title: Decoded #8: What a Year of Ads Taught Us: 2026 in Creative
hook: If you deleted every ad tomorrow, what would your brand still know?
caption:
If you deleted every ad your brand ran this year, what would you still know?

For most teams, the honest answer is: not much. The ads are in the account, the reports are in a folder, and the lessons are in someone's head.

In Issue #6 of Decoded, Raj looks back at 2026 in creative: the year Meta started reading ads instead of only ranking them, five lessons from the ads Galvor decoded, and five moves to make in the last two weeks of December so January doesn't start from zero.

# Decoded · Issue #6 — What a year of ads taught us: 2026 in creative
*Skeleton — Raj to write in full. ~1,500 words when finished.*

**Opening (Monday, 9:40 a.m.):** Sam's year-end review. The deck lists every campaign and every spend line. It doesn't list a single thing the brand learned. Sam asks: if we deleted all our ads tomorrow, what would we still know?

**Key takeaways (draft):**
1. 2026 was the year Meta started reading ads, not just ranking them (Andromeda, GEM, GenRecs — Issue #3).
2. The teams that improved fastest changed one attribute at a time and wrote down what they expected.
3. The most expensive mistake of the year was repeating a lesson already paid for.

**Section 1 — The platform year in one page.** Recap Meta's three rebuilt layers and the Creative diversity column (started late August, most accounts by the last week of October). What changed for a D2C team in practice. Only Meta's public claims from the facts bank.

**Section 2 — Five lessons from the ads Galvor decoded this year.** One lesson each from Issues #2–#5: false bangers (a high hook rate isn't a winner on its own); new buyers, not new looks (36% less for look-alikes; 47% more for a proven message in a new look); beyond narrative (attributes, not stories); fatigue has three causes; give new ads time (~35% dearer early, close to average over life).

**Section 3 — What Galvor saw in the data.** [DATA NEEDED: year-level view across the brands we work with — attribute that most often separated top-spending ads from the rest, by category; anonymised.] [DATA NEEDED: festive season (Oct–Nov) vs rest of year — did winning hooks change?]

**Section 4 — Festive season, looked at honestly.** What Diwali-period creative did differently in India this year: gifting moments, regional language, offer-led hooks. Use only patterns we can back up.

**Section 5 — The shift for marketers and leaders: five moves for the last two weeks of December.** (1) Write your brand's 10 lessons of 2026 on one page. (2) Delete the reports nobody acted on. (3) Pick the three attributes you'll test first in January. (4) Archive winners with their reasons, not just their files. (5) Agree one question for every post-mortem in 2027: "what did this ad teach us?"

**Close:** "Every ad should make the next one better." A year is long enough to check whether that happened.

**Next issue:** 2027 creative planning — build a test calendar, not a content calendar.
